claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 6 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Based on the information you've provided:

- You have a son, Alex, who is 6 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you

This means you meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK, and you're usually responsible for a child if you live with them.

Just a couple more questions to ensure there are no circumstances that might affect eligibility:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any form of residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually he was in care for a short while - just a couple of months earlier this year. But he's been back home with me since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. I need to understand this situation a bit better to assess eligibility accurately.

**Can you tell me more specifically:**
1. **How many weeks was Alex in care?**
2. **Is he now living with you full-time again, and if so, how long has he been back home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was about 7 weeks that he was in care. And yes, he's been back home with me full-time since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex was in care for 7 weeks (which is less than the 8-week threshold), and he's now back home living with you full-time, this shouldn't affect your eligibility.

Just one more question to complete the assessment:

**During those 7 weeks when Alex was in care, did he spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or were you regularly spending money on him (for things like clothes, presents, food, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, during those 7 weeks he was at the care home full-time - he didn't come home to stay with me during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have a complete picture of your situation.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have a 6-year-old son, Alex
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you full-time now
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He was in care for 7 weeks earlier this year (which is under the 8-week threshold that would typically affect eligibility)
- He is now back home with you full-time

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is 6 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you, which means you're responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- The 7-week period in care earlier this year doesn't affect your eligibility since it was under the 8-week threshold

You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex if you haven't already done so. 

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you would still be eligible to receive the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
